# In-World Texts — Koans, Fables, Apocrypha

The quotable corpus: material the narrator can read at a remove in cold opens and
outros ([[narrator-framing]]). Each specimen is one `##` section — a status marker, a
`> kind:` line naming its register, then one or more quotable passages written as
italic quotations. Plain-text paragraphs are editorial notes and are never read aloud.
No two episodes of an arc should quote the same source. Diegetic file: everything
here must pass the banned-vocabulary scan.

## The Fable of the Iron and the Thread

> status: provisional (D-0045)
> kind: fable

*"They say the Mountain of Chalk grew tired of holding up the sky, so it asked the
Valley for a pillar of iron. The Valley gave its iron. The Keep built its pillar. But
the heavier the iron became, the faster the sky fell, until the clouds dragged
through the mud. The Arch-Scribes calculated the weight of the sky, but they forgot
to calculate the weight of the pillar. It was only when a beggar tied a single,
hollow reed to the peak that the sky remembered how to float. A ledger can measure
gravity, but only an empty vessel can hold the wind."*

## The Apocrypha of the Eaten Word

> status: provisional (D-0045, D-0046)
> kind: apocrypha

*"A starving man asked the Scriptorium for bread. The Scribe, bound by the Ledger,
wrote the word 'Wheat' on a pristine piece of vellum and handed it to the man. The
man ate the vellum and died of Wyrd-rot. The Scribe was not punished for murder. He
was executed for wasting ink on a corpse. To the Ledger, the map is always more
valuable than the territory. To survive the Ledger, you must learn to eat the dirt."*

(Amended per D-0046: the original draft's final lines used a modern word; "the
Ledger" replaces it.)

## The Lesson of the False Measurement

> status: provisional (D-0230)
> kind: lesson

*"The Scribe asked the Skald: If the Wyrd is a river, how do you prove the water? The
Skald replied: You do not prove the water. You prove the thirst of the deer that
drinks from it. The Scribe, angered, dammed the river to measure its depth in still
iron. The water became a ledger. The deer died of thirst. And the river, possessing
no proof of its own existence, vanished into Wyrd-fog. Here ends the lesson of the
False Measurement. To name a thing without needing it is the genesis of all rot."*

## The Paradox of the Floating Quarry

> status: proposed
> kind: fable

*"When the Keep of the Valley demanded iron, the miners stripped the mountain's
bones. But the mountain did not weep. It simply forgot the treaty of gravity. A stone
that forgets it is heavy will fall upward; a man who forgets he is a guest will be
swallowed by the sky. Thus began the paradox of the Floating Quarry."*

(An earlier-style specimen; superseded in manner by the more impenetrable koan form
the author requested in D-0045 — kept as a fable-register example.)

## The Counting-Koans, Ninth of the Set, Taught Before a First Proof

> status: provisional (D-0230)
> kind: koan

*"A clerk was sent to number the bees of a hedge. He counted twice and got two sums,
so he stilled the hedge until the bees would hold their places. They held. He wrote
the true number and sealed it in wax. The hedge did not flower, and the parish ate
the count that winter. A tally holds still. Nothing that holds still is honey."*

## Mortar and Quickset, A Boundary Parable of the Hedge Country

> status: provisional (D-0230)
> kind: parable

*"Two brothers had fields of one size and boundaries of one length. One cut stone to
a single measure and mortared it, and then he slept, for the wall asked nothing of
him. One laid a hedge and bent it again every seventh year, and cursed it, for the
hedge asked him always. In the drought year the hare crossed the hedge and did not
cross the wall. Ask which brother owned a field, and which owned a fence."*

## The Water That Was Always There, A Fable Told Downstream of the Crags

> status: provisional (D-0230)
> kind: fable

*"The crags asked the lowlands to hold their washings a while, and the lowlands,
being neighborly, held them. The crags asked again, and again the lowlands held. At
length the crags sent a clerk to record that the water had always lain there. He
wrote it down. The lowlands sank, and the fringes drank what the lowlands could not
keep. No one upstream was ever wet. That is the whole of the argument, and it is
still being made."*

## The Second Pot, An Apocryphon Kept by the Hedge-Smiths

> status: provisional (D-0230)
> kind: apocrypha

*"A woman brought a stamped pot to the licensed forge and was told the mend would
cost more than the pot. She took it to a man under a hedge, who mended it for a loaf,
and the pot outlived them both. The keep hanged the man for the mend and not for the
pot. In the roll he is entered as a thief of labor. What he stole was the second
pot."*

## Schedule of Cutting, Reeds and Withies, Fourth Table

> status: provisional (D-0230)
> kind: quota-law

*"Of reeds. A parish shall cut what a parish is set. Where the water rises and the
reed is short, the parish shall cut what a parish is set. Where the cutters are
fewer, the parish shall cut what a parish is set. Nothing herein shall be read to
work hardship, the Plenty being sufficient to all who are counted. Appeals lie to the
keep that set the number."*

*"Of the sick. A cutter who cannot cut shall be carried on the roll one turning of
the moon, in the Plenty's kindness. Thereafter the parish shall make good the
shortfall, the parish having had the benefit of him. Nothing herein shall be read to
work hardship."*

## Deposition of a Midwife, Second Hearing

> status: provisional (D-0230)
> kind: testimony

*"They asked who taught me. I said my hands. They asked who taught my hands. I said
the woman before me, and they wrote her name down, and they asked who taught her. I
said the woman before her. They asked for how long. I said longer than your rolls.
They wrote that down as well, and there it is, in your own hand, in your own book.
Read it out."*

## A Stone That Was Never a Hearth, As the Hearthless Tell It

> status: provisional (D-0230)
> kind: parish-tale

*"When they were struck from the roll, the family carried the hearthstone out with
them, which is not permitted. They set it down at every camp. It never warmed
anything again. The aunt would not eat until it stood square. The children learned to
set it square, and their children set square a stone that had never been a hearth.
Ask the rolls where that family lives. The rolls say nowhere."*

## A Cutting-Song of the Reed Parishes

> status: provisional (D-0230)
> kind: work-song

*"One hand to the reed and one to the man beside you. Cut low and cut wet, and leave
the short ones standing. The bundle goes up to the keep by noon. The knot that holds
it was tied by four hands and is counted as none. Count what you like, sir. The
binding is here."*

## Against Rust, Kept Over the Doors of the Crag Country

> status: provisional (D-0230)
> kind: charm

*"Iron, you were dug and you were owed for. Iron, you were sung over and set in the
door. Iron, remember the hand and not the hoard. Speak the three lines whole and
speak them slow, and change no sound in them. The woman who taught them is dead, and
the reason went into the bog with her, and still the blade keeps."*

## Those the Roll Did Not Keep, A Keening Sung at the Pit-Mouths

> status: provisional (D-0230)
> kind: lament

*"We have no names for you, so we will say what you did. You carried. You bore. You
went down into the dark and came up in the dark and were counted at neither end. The
roll that held your names has been burned by the men who wrote it. We will say what
you did until somebody remembers what you were called. Sleep now. We are not
finished."*

## Nothing About Me But Stones, A Riddle Traded at the Hedge-Fairs

> status: provisional (D-0230)
> kind: riddle

*"Here is a riddle for the road. I am filled by many and opened by one. I stand on a
hill that grows no grain. Every year I am fuller and every year the hill is thinner,
and when at last I am full to the roof there will be nothing about me but stones.
What am I, and what will I be worth?"*

## The Man Who Never Drew the Debt, Told Against the Licensed Decks

> status: provisional (D-0230)
> kind: koan

*"A frightened man was given a clean deck by the keeps, and every leaf in it was
true. He laid a round and it came out kind. He laid another and it came out kind. He
laid rounds for forty years and never once drew the Debt, and he died grateful, in a
house that was not his, on a hill that had been a wood. Count the leaves. It is what
is not in a hand that reads it."*

## Two Crossings, Called the Ford Parable in the Low Country

> status: provisional (D-0230)
> kind: parable

*"Two came to the same ford in the same hour. One asked the water's leave and set
down a bit of bread he wanted for himself. He crossed, and the ford was a ford. One
read out the deed that said the crossing was his. He stepped in, and the ford was
water. Both of them got over. Only one of them can come back."*

## The Reckoning in the Ditch, A Fable the Keeps Do Not License

> status: provisional (D-0230)
> kind: fable

*"The keeps taught a boy a reckoning that always came out in their favor. When it
failed him, he understood that truth belonged to his betters. A woman in a ditch
taught him a reckoning that came out however the ground came out. The first time it
failed him, he understood that he had reckoned wrong. They hanged the woman for the
second lesson. The first is still taught, and it is free."*

## The Mill-Roll, Year of the Low Roofs, in a Second Hand

> status: provisional (D-0230)
> kind: chronicle

*"In that year the ice took the low roofs, and the keep's stores were sealed against
the count being spoilt. Item: eleven households went under one roof at the mill and
did not starve. Item: no proof was spoken, no rite was kept, nothing was mended.
Item: they were fined in the spring for the smoke of one fire where eleven were owed.
The fine is recorded. The winter is not."*

## She Would Not Be Helped, A Saying of Those Who Plant Late

> status: provisional (D-0230)
> kind: koan

*"They asked the old woman why she was setting a nut she would never see leafed. She
said the wood had been cut in her grandmother's time and she had been cold all her
life. They said that was not an answer. She said it was the whole answer, and went on
setting nuts, and would not be helped, and would not stop. There is a wood there now.
Nobody knows her name."*

## Aphorisms of the three creeds

> status: proposed
> kind: aphorisms

Repeated creed-phrases the three faiths use as callbacks and value-orientation — the
heard medium's substitute for a visible holy symbol. Grouped by culture; each carries a
one-line note on how it is used. None is ratified.

**The empire's scribes.**

- *"The Ledger balances."* — The chilling all-purpose justification: whatever was taken,
  the reckoning required it. Spoken the way a clean hand washes itself of a verdict.
- *"Ink over earth."* — A creed of supremacy: the written count outranks the living
  Wyrd. The motto of enclosure.
- *"Nothing uncounted, nothing unbound."* — A scribe's valediction and quiet threat; to
  be off the rolls is to be prey.

**The native animists.**

- *"The Wyrd remembers the weight."* — Ecological debt: every taking is recorded by the
  world itself and comes due. Both comfort and warning.
- *"No knot tied alone."* — The organizing line of the whole creed: magic and survival
  are shared, never solitary; mutual aid stated as folk wisdom.
- *"Leave the root, take the fruit."* — The rule of sustainable harvest, taught to
  children before they can reason a proof.

**The working poor.**

- *"Keep your head below the mist."* — Survival by going unnoticed; precisely the fearful
  habit the protagonist must unteach the apprentice.
- *"Cold iron pays the toll."* — When high reasoning fails, grounded physical reality
  keeps you alive; trust the ground under your feet over any clever word.

Two questions the creeds raise are recorded, not resolved: which native line the
protagonist forces the apprentice to repeat before their first proof, and how heavily
each creed leans on its aphorisms from region to region — matters for [[religion]] and
[[audio-design]] to settle.
